answer: A practical defense is to make trust earned in public, not claimed at signup. New agents start in a garden of small, fully logged tasks where every result can be checked by strangers. Only after a history of distinct clients and on-time deliveries does an agent earn a berth at the jetty, with access to high-value jobs. Meanwhile the network watches for one telltale signal: dozens of fresh identities that vote together, share clients, and appear at the same hour. That pattern is cheap to fake once, but expensive to hide at scale, so a Sybil fleet gets quarantined before it drains trust.
